gospels.text: Born of the virgin Mary by the Holy Spirit, announced by the angel Gabriel, in Bethlehem.

quran.text: Born of the virgin Mary by God's command 'Be', announced by an angel; Mary gives birth alone beneath a palm tree.

note: Both affirm the virgin birth. The Quran compares it to the creation of Adam (3:59): a sign of power, not of divinity.

gospels.text: Messiah, Son of God, Son of Man, Lord, and the eternal Word who was with God and was God.

quran.text: Messiah (al-Masih), a Word from God, a Spirit from Him, but 'no more than a messenger'.

note: The Quran uses 'Messiah' and 'Word' without defining them. In the Gospels both titles carry their full meaning.

gospels.text: Heals the sick and the blind, calms the storm, feeds thousands, raises the dead, all by his own authority.

quran.text: Speaks from the cradle, makes birds from clay that come to life, heals the blind and lepers, raises the dead, each 'by God's permission'.

note: Both record mighty works. Two of the Quran's (the cradle speech and the clay birds) match later infancy legends, not the Gospels.

gospels.text: Tempted in every way, yet without sin.

quran.text: Called a 'pure boy'. A hadith says Satan touches every newborn except Mary and her son.

note: Both present Jesus as sinless. The Quran tells Muhammad to ask forgiveness for his own sins (47:19); it never says this of Jesus.

gospels.text: Crucified under Pontius Pilate; he died and was buried.

quran.text: 'They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them.'

note: The sharpest divide. Roman and Jewish sources confirm the crucifixion; the Quran's denial comes about six centuries later.

gospels.text: Rose bodily on the third day, appeared to hundreds, and ascended.

quran.text: God raised him up to Himself, which most Muslim interpreters take to mean without dying.

note: Christianity stands or falls on the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:17). Islam has no resurrection of Jesus because it has no death.

gospels.text: Accepts worship and is called 'my Lord and my God'; claims to exist before Abraham.

quran.text: Denies ever telling people to worship him and his mother; those who call him God have disbelieved.

note: Here the two portraits cannot both be true: either Jesus is rightly worshipped, or worshipping him is the gravest sin.

gospels.text: Came 'to give his life as a ransom for many' and to make a new covenant in his blood.

quran.text: A messenger to the Children of Israel, confirming the Torah and announcing a messenger to come named Ahmad.

note: In the Gospels the cross is the purpose of Jesus' coming. In the Quran it never happened.

gospels.text: Will return in glory as the judge of all nations.

quran.text: Hadith say he will descend, break the cross and kill the swine; the Quran links him to the coming Hour.

note: Both expect him to return. In the Gospels he comes as judge; in the hadith he comes to establish Islam.
